messages.content:
Chapter One 

I awoke slowly. I swear I had heard something coming from the hallway just outside the room, a knock of some sorts. Or maybe not, I’m still half asleep. Just as I am being swallowed up back into my dreams I hear it again, this time louder and more clear. I sit up, being careful not to wake my wife next to me. I stay there and listen for awhile. A few minutes pass while I listen attentively. It’s just the house settling, I tell myself, it is ancient after all. My wife stirs next to me in her sleep, making me tired again. I lay back down hoping that this time no strange sounds would wake me up again. 

I woke up a few hours later to an empty bed and the faint smell of coffee. Sharlene was always up before me brewing a pot. Every morning was perfect with her, she was the one I could confide in, she was the one who believed in me and got me to where I am today, but most importantly, she was my best friend. The cold floor felt amazing against my feet as I walked to the doorway. I stopped in and stretched out my arms against its wooden frame and started thinking about the reasons that brought me to this house. I despised the heat which was a major factor in us moving here closer to the mountains and away from the city. That and the noise of the city was way too big of a distraction for someone like me. 

I remember the day I came home from the music hall, angry with myself and the life God had given me. Sharlene sat there and listened, absolving me of all my guilt and shame that I had for myself. Back then I had a big sleeping issue, now before you think to yourself “Oh what about that knocking you heard last night? Surely that has something to do with your sleeping issue returning!” No, it doesn’t, it’s an old house and everyone knows old houses make noises, albeit strange noise, but still just noises. 

Anyways, I digress, Sharlene was there that day and pointed out the obvious. The reasons behind my shitty mood were two-fold. First, the house we were living in was situated right by the tracks and one of the main roads. Imagine you are trying to get some peace and quiet and all you hear is iron horses on twisted tracks and semi-trucks blasting down the road because they’re about to piss themselves and the truck stop is only ten minutes away! 

Now secondly, and perhaps most importantly, was my mother’s passing. She was a sweet lady, a lot like Sherlene, and I can recall that day that changed our lives so clearly, like it’s still happening in this moment. 

.	.	. 

 

“Hector your mom is waiting in the car, I thought you were ready an hour ago!” Said Sherlene. I fumbled with my tie, rushing to get the perfect knot in only a few seconds, like a personal world record.  

“She’s fine honey! I was ready but my other tie looked like a vomit stain on my chest, who the hell buys a green and yellow colored tie? I must’ve been high when I picked this out.” 

“That was a birthday gift from Darren.” She places both her hands on my shoulders and starts gently pushing me out the bathroom door and toward the front door, but not before she kisses me on the cheek. “Your tie looks great now, let’s go.” She smiles and continues to guide me, this time through the living room full of furniture older than me. 

“Thank you baby.” I say to her, all the while thinking how Darren, my cousin, was a prick for picking me out that tie and making me late all these months later. 

We’re finally out of the house now and I turn to lock the front door as Sherlene gets in the passanger seat. I walk around to the driver side, the sun beaming down on the black car makes it look like a void swallowing all the rays. An intimidating black that screams “I spent all my money on this car and still live with my mom!” I laugh a little bit at my situation and get inside, put it in reverse, and back out the cracked drive way. A train whistle blows and startles me, causing to almost hit a car coming my way. They lay down on their horn and the sound intermingles with the train horn, creating a blaring choir that had no warning, no crescendo, just an annihilation by sound that stabs through me and pisses me off. 

The look on my mother’s face says it all before she even spoke. “Pay closer attention Hector! You just about ruined your car!” That was her polite way of saying, I can’t believe your idiocy almost cost me my life. 

I  dismiss the incident as best I can and start driving down the road, passing nicely planted trees on the sidewalk, window shoppers, dog walkers, and the occasional pot smoking hippie. 

“It’s been a while since we’ve been to Al’s Bird Cage isn’t?” said mom, her smile puffing up her cheeks. 

“Ma it’s been like two weeks.” I reply 

“That is pretty long babe, especially when it’s usually a weekly ritual.” Said Sharlene. 

“See Hector, at least Sharlene knows when its been a while! We should go again right away next week, before the birds are gone for the season.” Sharlene turns around and nods at mom in agreeance. They both love the colorful birds at the restaurant and we almost never go when they’ve been put away when the seasons change and it gets too hot or cold for them. 

“They should have an indoor spot for the birds.” I say. Sherlene scrunches her face at me. 

“Bird feathers and poop? In a restaurant? That would put them out of business real quick.” She says. 

“Definitely quicker than it takes for Hector to get ready!” Laughs my mother, Sherlene joining in on the fanfare. I start laughing too at my mom’s wit, a good indicator that she’s still in good health for her age, a thought that I would soon come to find out betrayed me. 

 

.	.	. 

 

I gasp, I can’t keep reliving it anymore, the smell of coffee fills my nose once again, brining me back to the present and grounding me in my new home, my new life. I still hear shuffling in the kitchen downstairs and then the sudden popping and sizzling noise that bacon makes when it first touches the hot pan. I take a moment to get my bearings before heading downstairs. I hate when my wife sees me like this, she’s done so much for me already and I hate having burden her. Though I know she would say something like, tell me what you’re going through I can help! And she can help, but I just wish I was able to help myself together for once. 

Ok. Stop getting caught up in emotion. Put on a happy face and go downstairs, everything will be alright. 

I finally take the first step out of the bedroom doorway and into the long hall. The dark oak walls paired with an equally dark wood flooring comforted me as I walked down to the stairs. The occasional small rug cushioned my feet on my journey, like little warm islands in a sea of coldness. The rugs were Sherlenes’ idea, she hated walking to the kitchen in the morning on a chilly floor unlike me, so the rugs became a sort of compromise between us. 

The walls in the hall were littered with old artistic paintings and black and white photos. It looks really bleak, but it lets me hone in on my music when I pass them. I continue down the hall passing an occasional door to a bathroom, bedroom, or closet until I reach the stairs. 

“Babe I hear you up there! Come get your coffee before it gets cold.” I heard Sherlene call from the kitchen. 

I walk down the stairs and into another small room that’s connected to the kitchen, a room that looks much more uplifting than any of the rooms upstairs, except our bedroom. Downstairs is Sherlenes’ domain, where she decorated it with lots of light colored furniture, plants, and open windows for natural light. It was pure and open, just like her. 

I walk into the kitchen and see her sitting at the table with a cup of coffee in front of her and another one in front of an empty chair. She looks up at me and smiles, a beautiful smile that sends a warmth through me. I smile back instinctively. Even if I was in the shittiest mood in the world, even if I was on a downward spiral into anger or apathy, her smile would always make me happier, as if it was some type of spiritual magic or something. In a way she was addicting. 

“Good morning babe, how’d you sleep.” I said, moving behind her chair and kissing her neck while I wrap my arms around her. 

She reaches up with one free hand and places it on my arm as I continue to hug her. “I slept just fine next to you.” She said, her head turned toward me, her eyes closed in bliss, that same smile shooting rays of warmth into my very being. 

“I slept good too. Except I woke up once in the middle of the night.” I said moving toward my chair and coffee. I sit down and reach across for it, taking a sip. I look up toward Sherlene, her eyes screening my face. Her eyebrow was raised in a questioning expression. 

“Oh really? What for?” 

I know what she’s really trying to ask. Did I just wake up by chance or is my mental anguish making a triumphant return. In a way I’m glad how she tiptoes around subjects like that, I hate being bombarded with emotional questions out of nowhere, it gives me a tendency to shut down. 

“I thought I hear a noise in the hallway.” 

I see her face relax a little. 

“Must have been the house settling, I mean just you walking down here sounded like a damn  thunderstorm with all the creaking.” Said Sherlene, her smile returning once again. 

“Yeah it creaks a shit ton, but get this” I say, as I lean forward toward her, “It sounded like someone knocking.” 

“Oh shut up you’re scaring me!” Her smile grew even wider and she laughed. 

“No no, I’m serious!” I laugh a little too, making it even harder to convince her it was real. 

“Okay, no joke. Are you messing with me?” She said. 

“I’m not!” 

“Hector.” She said, stretching out the last half of my name. 

“I’m dead serious Sherlene.” 

“Oh good we’re living in a haunted house now! I would never survive in a real life horror movie babe, you know I don’t even enjoy watching them like you do.” We were both laughing again. Now that I think about it, the house being old it was most definitely the pipes. 

“So, what would you like to do today?” Said Sherlene. “You don’t have practice right?” 

“Nope, I’m free, I’m down to do whatever you want.” I said. She pondered a little bit before speaking again. 

“Maybe we can go out to eat somewhere? Like a date night!” 

“That sounds great babe! What should we do until then?” 

“Well, I have some work to do in the garden, why don’t we meet back up again for lunch?” 

I agree and we finish our coffee together. After Sherlene says her momentary goodbye and kisses me, I head back upstairs. Even though I may not have full rehearsals with the orchestra today I still need to practice by myself. If I am being honest, even if I had no longer had a seat in the orchestra, even if I had an entirely different career at this point, I still would never be able to stop playing, it’s like and obsession at this point.  

The practice room upstairs mimicked the rest of the long hallway used to reach it. The interior of the room was lined with dark wood for both the walls and the floors. Art hung upon the walls projecting a kind of sadness and despair into the air. A kind of concoction of darkness that I feel at home in. 

The room is furnished with a singular mahogany desk, its knobs made of a polished brass and encrusted with fine stones, and a matching chair, masterfully carved. At the northern side of the room is a window that reaches from the bottom of the floor to the ceiling, closed with drapes of a brutally dark red, swirls of golden thread decorate the drapes in a dazzling display of great design. In the center of the room sits a beautiful wooden chair, much like the one at the desk, a violin case, and a music stand. 

I keep my practice room pristine, both in cleanliness and décor. This is my true home, my sanctuary, the place my true spirit comes out and battles with itself and my damaged mind. I need it to stay like this, it’s for the best. 

I walk over to the window and pull the drapes apart. Usually I would keep them closed, but the winter season brought with it an almost constant overcast. I unlatched the brass lock on the window and swung it open, breathing in the fresh, cold air. 

Beautiful. 

I take my seat in the center of the room and reach down to the violin case. I pick it up and place it in my lap, running my hand across its smooth surface. I smile as I undo the clips and take it out. 

It’s an astonishing instrument, from its handcrafted shape to its delicate strings. I love it like a father loves a child. 

I prop it up and gently place the bow onto the strings. I push and pull ever so slightly, starting slow into my music. A sorrowful yet beautiful sound begins to come out. I keep playing as the cold air blows across my skin, energizing me, I start to pick up the tempo. The sorrowful turns into a haunting melody that fills the air of the room, I keep going, entranced in my obsession once again. The macabrely enchanting music keeps filling the room, until it is buzzing with energy and I am sucked in deeper and deeper. My playing grows faster and more demanding, more horrific, and more divine. The air in the room crackles with the sounds of my music and I am lost in the instrument, my mind goes black though I can feel myself keep playing. 

 

.	.	. 

 

“Hector right here honey!” Said Mother. With enthusiasm and excitement in her voice she points to a parking spot close to Al’s Bird Cage. She was pretty upset last week when we didn’t make it. I ended up having extra rehearsals that week right before the concert, but I promised her I’d try and make sure we wouldn’t miss a single week when the birds come back next season. 

I feel myself getting quite hungry and excited too as I pull into the parking spot and shut off the car. I turn to my passengers, my beautiful wife, Sherlene, and my dear Mother, and give them a smile. 

“Are you girls hungry or what?” I said. Nods of agreement ensued. 

I got out quickly and rushed to the passeneger side door, my mother was already out of the car and Sherlene had the door slightly opened as she unclipped her seat belt. 

“Not so fast!” I said, closing Sherlene’s door again, only to reopen it with a smile. 

“Oh aren’t you just such a gentleman!” She said and giving a chuckle. I grabbed her by the arm and led the three of us up to the front door. 

The outside to Al’s Bird Cage was beautiful. Decorated with vines growing up the beige brick walls, short iron fences sectioning it off from the rest of the side walk and other stores nearby, and various paintings showcasing the different birds they had. 

The room inside was only used as a gift shop and restrooms, that’s also where the hostess booth was. All the birds were outside like Sherlene had mentioned earlier. The hostess greeted us with a smile and asked how many there were. 

“Three, please!” My mother replied. Her happiness was just as contagious as Sherlene’s smile. It’s no wonder why I love them both so dearly. 

“Right this way.” Said the hostess, leading us out to the garden area. We walked down a stone path, the walls were fairly close with more vines clinging to them. We could hear the birds singing their songs in the afternoon air as the path opened up to a large seating area. 

There were white painted benches, fountains, and bird cages everywhere. An outside bar featuring various different spiked teas and coffees. As well as an expansive garden with small creeks an little stone bridges to wander through while waiting for your food or after you eat. 

Eventually we were seated under a white gazebo with two small bird cages and a third, larger one. The two smaller ones had different colored finches inside and the third appeared to be some kind of white parrot, its beak almost as big as my hand. As we watched the birds flutter around their homes our server approached and took our order of drinks. 

Long Island Iced Tea for me, a water for my Sherlene, and an Arnold Palmer for my mother. 

“So Hector, how has work been?” Said Mother, clasping her hands under the table and leaning forward in interest. 

“I would hardly call it work. I love it so much, to just sit back and get paid to do what I love.” I said. 

“Do you ever feel like getting paid to do what you love takes the magic out of it?” Said Sherlene. 

“Nothing could take the magic out of what I do. They always say ‘Do what you love and you’ll never work a day’ or something like that, and I have to agree with that. It’s easy. It pays well. I got a good thing going.” I said. 

“Well I’m just glad you’re happy.” Said my mother, smiling at me. 

“And what about you Sherlene, how is work?” Said Mother, taking another sip of her drink. 

“Oh you know, it’s nice. I wouldn’t really compare it to Hector’s luckiness though,” she flashes me a smile and I feel warmth in my body, “No but it’s good, I’m happy working for the police department.” 

“Any strange calls lately?” I ask. Sherlene looks over at the birds and scrunches her face in thought. Working as a dispatcher she usually has at least one or two weird or awful calls a month. 

“Well,” She clears her throat, “I’m gonna laugh as I say this but, we got a call just the other day from a young man who...let's just say put a part of himself somewhere it didn’t belong and got it stuck!” Me an Sherlene burst out with laughter. My mom just sits there confused. 

“What like a finger? That’s not too bad!,” She pauses for a moment and I see the realization cross her face, “Oh my lord not his….oh dear!” She starts to laugh as well and her face turns red. 

“That actually reminds me of a time that Hector had…” 

“Mom no! Now isn’t the time!” I said. Interrupting whatever embarrassing story she was about to tell Sherlene. 

 

.	.	. 

 

I suddenly awoke from the blackness of my haunting memory by a loud knocking in the hallway. My head was throbbing and I was dripping in sweat. I got up from the floor and put my violin back in its case before quickly walking to the door and flinging it open. 

Where the fuck is this noise coming from? 

I pace the halls and fling open more doors. I’m confused and angry now. This knocking, these memories, are all just toying with my mind. I walk back into the practice room and go to shut the window, I see Sherlene down below still working in her garden, completely unaware of my most recent episode, I plan to keep it that way. I sit back down in the chair at the center of the room and try to relax before heading back downstairs. 

Maybe helping Sherlene in the garden will ease my mind. 

After a few minutes I get up and go downstairs, leaving through the kitchen door into the backyard. I walk around the side of the house into the garden where Sherlene notices me. 

“I heard you practicing upstairs babe, it sounded good! A little haunting, but good!” She smiled at me. Her smile, I know I’ve said it so many times before but I’ll say it again, her smile is contagious. I instantly feel better and I even laugh a little bit as I run up and hug her. 

“Why’d you end up stopping? That was barely twenty minutes.” She said, brushing dirt off her gloves. 

“I realized I’d rather spend this time with you in the garden.” I looked deep in her eyes and ran my hand up her arm before pulling her in for a kiss. Her lips were soft against mine and I could feel her breath getting faster. I moved my hand to the side of her neck and pulled her in even tighter. We stayed like that for awhile before we broke away. 

For the next hour we worked in the garden, transplanting some flowers, and covering some bushes for the cold weather we had coming our way. I also thankfully remembered to wrap the outside pipes so we could still have running water in the morning. After we finished up with the garden we looked around outside to see if there was anything else that we could do. We ended up gathering sticks and branches to put in the shed for a fire tonight. 

“I think that’s good baby.” Said Sherlene. I nodded and motioned toward the house. 

“We better go shower before we go out.” I said. We walked across the yard and onto the front porch before going inside.  

The front of the house was also decorated by Sherlene, the front has a beautiful stone walkway leading up to the front porch that she had picked out at the local hardware store that me and Derreck had installed a couple of months ago. The front porch had an arrainment of potted plants like monkey grass, onion rings, and fizddlehead fern. There was also a nice bright set of matching patio furniture and wind chimes. It was a great place to sit outside and drink while enjoying the rural scenery. 

Once inside we walked upstairs from the main living room and turned right down the long hallway until we reached a large bathroom. The bathroom was dimly lit unlike the master bathroom that needed to be brighter for us to get ready in. This bathroom however, was meant more for a shower with two people in it. 

The bathroom walls and floor were made up with dark brown tiles. A marble sink was built into the wall and an expansive mirror was set right above it. The shower was also tile and was in the shape of an ‘L’. Where’d you pull the curtain back, walk in and take a small right to the shower head. It was definitely made for a couple forever trapped in the honey moon phase, a couple like us. I took off my shoes and walked into the shower to let the water heat up. We undressed while we waited then stepped inside. 

Sherlene’s skin was still glowing from the sun outside. Sweat clinged to her body and intermingled with the hot water before finally being washed away. Swells of steam signifying their departure	down the shower drain. 

She’s beautiful. 

I feel my worries and despair slip down the drain after looking at her. Just like the hot water cleans our flesh, she cleans my fucked up inner world.  

We stare into each other’s eyes as I reach my hand out, she notices and takes it, placing it on her chest. My hand is gentle and firm around her. 

I turn my hand over and glide my knuckles softly from her shoulder down to her wrist. I can feel goosebumps forming on her through the steam. 

She is my everything, my entire life and reason for living. 

The rest of the day goes by faster than expected and before I know it we’re getting into the car for our date night. I pull out the driveway and we make our way through the dark roads into the city. Every street lamp I pass under lights up the cab, illuminating Sherlene. My hand lays in her lap, while her fingers intertwine with mine. 

We get to the restaurant, a nice little Italian place downtown, and wait to be seated. It wasn’t too busy here at the time, a nice bonus. The host leads us to a booth in the corner of the dimly lit dinning room and hand us the menus. 

“Your server will be right with you,” he said, walking away. 

“This place is cute isn’t it? I bet your mom would’ve liked it.” Said Sherlene. 

I look up at her, emotions running high at just the mention of my mother, “Let’s not talk about her.” 

“Hector it’s been months since it happened and you never mention her. I know it was awful, but part of the reason you feel depressed all the time is because you ignore it.” She said. 

“Quit trying to be my damn therapist!” I was thankful it wasn’t busy and we had the booth in the back, otherwise I would have been more embarrassed that I already was. 

Sherlene stirred in her seat and I could feel the mood deteriorating fast, “I’m sorry, I just worry about you.” She got up and walked toward the restrooms. I swear I saw tears rolling down her face as she walked away. I sat there alone, feeling like a terrible person. She didn’t do anything wrong and I know she’s right, I need to move on. 

 

.	.	. 

 

My mother laid back and let out a long groan before looking up at me and Sherlene, “That was just delicious as always.” She paused for a moment, “You know what time it is now don’t you?” 

“Of course!” Said Shelene standing up and making her way to the start of the garden path. 

“This has to be my favorite part.” Said Mom, “After the birds of course!” The three of us wandered the path, taking in the sights and sounds of the landscape before us. An array of colorful flowers bloomed all around and the sweet smell of wet grass filled the air. The chirping of all the different birds was like a great concert made specifically for us. 

As we continue to walk along the garden I notice something a little off about Mom, she keeps smirking, not the usual smile she has when enjoying the gardens, but almost as if she’s keeping some kind of secret. I stop abruptly	and wait for the two of them to turn around. 

“What’s the hold up.” Said Mom, still with that smirk on her face. 

“I feel like there’s something you want to say Mom, why else would you keep on smiling like that?” 

Mom let out a laugh and threw up her hands like she’d been caught breaking into a safe, “Okay, okay, you got me. That’s why I never gambled with your dad, terrible poker face!” She motioned with her hand for me to come closer to the two of them. 

“Hector,” Said Mom grabbing me by the shoulders, “What if I told you; You and Sherlene, Me, Marge and Derreck, are all going on a vacation!” 

“I would say, ‘Wow a vacation, that’s awesome, but how is it a vacation with Derreck!’ Then I guess I would ask where to or something like that.” I said. 

“Oh be quite, Derreck isn’t that bad, certainly not bad enough to ruin a vacation,” Said Sherlene. 

“Wait a second, wait just a second! You were in on this weren’t you! I should have known something was up, what with all the questions about upcoming concerts and practice.” I said. The thought of a vacation started to sound more appealing, with or without Dickhead Derreck. 

“Want to know where to?” Said Mom, leaning in for the grand reveal and to catch my reaction to whatever it is she’s going to say. 

I nod, anticipating either something crazy like Moscow or something lame like the local them park and their three broken rides from the 80’s. 

“We’re going to, duh duh duh! Shermont Lake!” She said with a little jump, throwing back her hands. Sherlene started clapping and cheering. 

“Where the hell is Shermont Lake.” Sherlene shot me glance, “Oh, Shermont Lake! How awesome, thanks Mom!” Sherlene gives a thumbs-up to me and I laugh. 

Mom lightly smacks me on the arm, “Oh don’t be such an ass, it’s a nice lake, we even have some cabins reserved for us!” 

“As long as I’m not sharing one with Dereck I’ll be fine.” I said. 

 

.	.	. 

 

I shake my head and my vision starts to clear up. 

I’m sitting at dinner with Sherlene, everything is fine. There’s nothing to worry about. 

Except there is something to worry about, Sherlene was still gone. I can never recall how much time has passed when the memories take over, sometimes it’s a minute, sometimes hours. I look around at the table, there’s no drinks on it so I’m guessing not much time has passed	at all. 

Out of curiosity and concern for my wife I get up and walk to the restrooms, they’re single rooms so she should be the only one in there. I press my ear up to the door and I can hear her talking to someone on the phone. I press harder to try and make out what she’s saying. 

“It’s not getting better for me.” Is one phrase I make out, I keep trying to listen, my heart thumping in my chest. “It was his mom. Yeah, I know. Okay, I’ll talk to you later. I miss you.” I hear her end the call and start coming toward the door, I awkwardly job back to the table and act like I wasn’t just eavesdropping on her. 

Who the fuck could she be sharing all this personal stuff about me with? Who’s consoling her other than me? And who the hell does she seem to miss so much? 

My thoughts are running rampant and I hear the bathroom door open. My heart is obliterating itself against my chest and I feel anger inside, who could she have been talking to. 

Okay just calm down and think. Who could she miss, probably one of her parents or her sister right? She still keeps in contact with them, after all she still has close family that’s alive. 

The rest of the dinner was strange. I was torn up inside, my thoughts convincing me she was some how cheating, while I also reasoned with myself that she wouldn’t, she couldn’t do something like that. I can tell she was so sad the entire time. I wanted to comfort her, but I couldn’t even comfort myself. 

The dive back home wasn’t any better, though the tears on her face made no noise, they were louder than the highway. 

 

Chapter Two 

The tires crush the gravel driveway as I pull in. Sherlene and I haven’t said a word to each other this whole time. I’m not even sure how to get a conversation started when we’re in this kind of mood. I figure that if I just wait long enough she’ll start it for me and that’s one less thing that I have to worry about. 

Sometimes I think that my lack of emotional maturity is a huge fault in our marriage, but am I really less mature or just ignorant? I know what you may be thinking right now, “Oh quit being a baby, grow some balls and comfort your damn wife, get on with this pathetic sob story!” Well you’re right, but it’s just not that simple for me, believe me. 

“Sherlene?” I finally open my mouth since we firsts sat down to dinner. My throat is dry and my voice sounds uneasy. She looks at me , halfway in the master bedroom, getting ready to take off her evening face she worked so hard to put together for our date that ended up being a shit show. 

“What is it Hector?” She said. I watched her chin tremble, yet her voice remained firm. I know I fucked up, enough time has passed since the incident that I should be able to talk about my mom without completely freaking out about it. 

“I’m sorry.” I say pathetically. I rub my hand on the back of my head and look at the floor, thinking carefully about what I’m going to say next. She leans her slender body against the door frame and crosses her arms over her chest. 

“It’s okay, I overreacted. I just wish you could be more open with me about how you’re feeling. I knew something was off about you today again. I should have just kept my distance instead of egging you on to talk when you’re not ready to.” 

“No, no, please. Don’t be sorry. Enough time has passed to where I should be able to talk about it. I don’t know why it’s tearing me up inside more than I’d like to admit to. But that’s not all…” I said, leaving my last words on a sort of cliff hanger. Hoping that we switch the topic from my mother over to the strange things that’s been taking place around the house. 

“What else is it baby?” She moved off the door frame and closer to me, placing a warming hand on my shoulder and looking at me with those caring, yet inquisitive eyes. 

“This morning I relived the memory of that day,” I said, “it was about my mom.” Sherlene kept her hand resting on me, signaling me to go on. “It wasn’t just once though. It happened again while I was practicing, then again in the restaurant when you walked away.” I put my head down shamefully. 

Why do I have to be so fucked up. I’m just a burden to her, offering nothing but a broken mind. 

“It’s okay baby, just talk about whatever you’re comfortable with.” She Said. I walked away from her and sat on the edge of the bed, my head in my hands. I thought how I should describe the physical effects of the “dreams” or whatever you would call them. I even considered bringing up the noises I heard when I woke up from my episode in the practice room.  

“It was like I lost my mind and had to relive the moment again.” I said. I let out a sigh and kicked my shoes off. 

I need a shower. And some damn sleep that hopefully doesn’t get interrupted by stupid knocking. 

I stand up and walk over to my wife, hugging her. I bury my face in her neck feeling her hair tickle my face. We embrace each other for some time and I feel myself calming down. The scent of her hair is inviting and I hug her tighter, hoping that it will be all over now, no more memories, no more sleep issues. Just a life of peace. 

We eventually break away from each other and head for the shower. The warm water makes me tired and I’m more than ready for sleep now. After we’re done showering we get into bed together. The satin black sheets and heavy blankets makes falling asleep so easy. I barely let out a “goodnight” before slipping away. 

 

.	.	. 

 

After our walk in the garden at Al’s Bird Cage we made our way home to relax and lounge around the house for the rest of the day. The tracks nearby were loud with activity as I parked in the driveway. Annoyed as always when the trains pass through, which is pretty regularly, I open the car door for Sherlene and walk her to the front door. I fumble with the keys for a moment, passing keys for a storage unit, a locker, the symposium hall, the shed in the backyard, until finally finding the right one. The key is hard to fit in the bronze door knob and requires a kind of shake to actually get the lock to turn. 

When we walk inside the house is colder than usual and Mom wastes no time to get to the thermostat. I take a seat next to Sherlene on the living room sofa and prop my feet up on the coffee table. A pile of DVDs sit in Sherlene’s lap as she looks for a movie to put on. 

Mom walks back in after fixing the temperature and hands me a pamphlet. “Open it up. It has all the information for the trip!” 

“Oh thanks I was wondering what the cabins would look like.” I said. I looked closer at the brochure and saw a picture of the lake with cabins spread out over the shoreline. They looked nicer than I was expecting. The brochure featured several different activities like canoeing, horseback riding, and guided nature walks. 

Plenty of activities means plenty of chances to avoid Dereck. 

“I hope you two enjoy it. It’s good to take time off and enjoy yourselves instead of being too occupied with work” She said, shooting a glance at me, “Especially if your work takes away from Al’s Bird Cage with your own mother!” She laughed and Sherlen joined in as well. 

“You make a good point. Hopefully Hector takes it to heart!” Said Sherlene, holding up a movie, “How about this one?” Mom nodded in approval at the movie Sherlene picked out. 

“Looks good! I’ll go start the popcorn.” Said Mom. She walked off into the kitchen and left me and Sherlene alone together. 

“So how long have you known about the lake trip?” I said, helping her put away all the movies she pulled out. 

“Only a week or two.” She responded, “Why?” 

“I really don’t want to see Dereck. He thinks he’s better than everyone else just because he went to some expensive special school for teeth. Everybody hates dentists so I guess he choose a career that suits him.” 

“Come on Hector, he isn’t that bad.” 

“Why do you stick up for him? Tell me he’s not annoying when he talks. You know what I’m talking about, how he exaggerates every story he tells. ‘Oh I’m Dereck I saved an infant from falling out a window on my way to buy groceries cause I’m a fucking super hero.’ He’s a load of shit is what he is.” 

“Babe I don’t think he ever talked about saving an infant, what are you going on about?” She said with a smile on her face. 

“He has a bigger house than me and rubs it in, fuck that guy.” I said. 

“Is that what this is about? His house?” 

“It’s a part of it.” 

“Well you know what you have that he doesn’t?” She said, leaning in close to whisper in my ear. 

“What’s that?” 

“Me.” She said. 

Goosebumps spread over my arm and I kissed her. Things were escalating quickly. I carresed her thigh over her sun dress before pulling it back and placing my hand directly on her skin. 

“Ahem. You might need to find a new place that isn’t the living room Hector.” Said Mom. I shot up flustered, completely forgetting she was just making popcorn and not out doing a spin class or whatever she does in her free time away from the house. 

“Oops I kind of forgot you were still here.” I said. I grabbed the movie Sherlene picked out and put it into the DVD player. 

 

.	.	. 

 

The house was dead silent, more than usual. I lay awake staring at the ceiling. Even my dreams are infected with the same memory now. I sat up and looked around. Thinking about way to ease my mind and help me get back to sleep. I would wake up Sherlene, but she needs to be up early for work in the morning and I know I would hate to be woken up if I was her. Besides, I troubled her enough as it wa today. 

I decided to just get up and go into the kitchen for a small snack or some w Truthfully I didn’t need anything and I wasn’t hungry at all, but maybe it could miracoulisly take my mind off of the torment I keep having to endure. 

 I check the time on my phone ‘3:15’ it read. I sighed and carefully lifted the sheets, exposing my skin to the cold air. Standing up slowly, I crept my way out the door and down the hall toward the stairs. The hallway looks so long in the dark and creepier than usual with the new moon. 

I turn the walk from the bedroom to the staircase a more leisurely stroll like a young mom pushing a stroller in a park. I stop at each painting and run my fingers across the edges,  taking in as much of the art as I can. The first painting features a young woman, her shoulder length hair painted with the finest strokes, her face is turned to the side as if she’s looking at something outside the frame. Her expression always seems to change for me. I asked Sherlene if she ever noticed it but she just chalked it up to my creative persona and a slightly overactive imagination. 

Sometimes she looks like she’s mesmerized by someone she loves, other times she looks a cross between puzzled and inquisitive. Yet no matter how she looks, she always reminds me of my wife, which is no surprise the main reason I bought it. I take one last look at it before moving on to the next one. 

On my way to the next painting I notice the air getting colder and I can feel a breeze. I look further down the hall and see the dark drapes move slightly. As I get closer I notice the window slightly opened letting in the cold air. 

Sherlene usually opens this one window in particular since it has a way of brightening my “gloomy” hallway. I can see why she favors this one, the view is great, but not just that. It’s weird to describe but the kitchen juts outwards a few feet toward the garden, so if I wanted to I could crawl out this window and be standing atop the kitchen roof. Which I may have done a few times with the violin, especially on bright nights. 

I take in the view from the window. The sea of trees impose themselves on the distant hills and sway in the breeze. While looking out across the yard a figure catches my attention, it’s hard to notice from all the way up here and especially since it’s so dark out, but it looked like a person running into the trees. 

What the hell was that? 

 I keep looking outside and begin to scan the backyard and the garden below. I don’t see anyone or anything else.  

Perfect, my sleep issues are coming back and now I’m hallucinating, what else can go wrong with me. 

I brush it off and close the window before I go downstairs, still feeling uneasy. The dark house doesn’t make it any better so I decide to turn on all the kitchen lights. All that darkness made it feel like I was being watched and that’s the last thing I want to be feeling right now. I slowly open a cabinet next to the stove, making sure to be as quiet as possible. I sort through several bags of chips, tuna cans, granola bars, and cookies before making my pick. 

I pull out a plastic bag of cookies and head to the kitchen table. I make it only three steps before I drop the bag. My heart is pounding because for a split second a shadow dashed across the yard and toward the trees, just like the first. 

Holy shit. Okay, there’s no way I can brush this one off. Could it be some sort of animal? But what kind of animal looks like it runs on its hind legs. 

Acting quickly I run to the light switch and smack it down so I can get a better view out the window, completely disregarding the amount of noise I’m making. I peer outside but see nothing. I gather up the courage to walk outside on the back porch and investigate further. A stupid decision, I know, but curiosity was getting the better of me. The kitchen door starts to creak as I open it and the porch groans with every step I take, so much for stealth. 

The night air was colder than usual and the breeze blowing through the trees didn’t help either. It was impossible to see if anything out there was moving because of the wind and the lack of moonshine. 

It’s gotta be my sleep. I need rest. Fuck getting this worked up over something that’s probably just a squirrel. 

“Hector?” 

I turn around fast and see Sherlene’s outline in the kitchen doorway. 

I catch my breath and feel relived it wasn’t a terrifying entity come to kill me like in a shitty horror film. “Holy hell Sherlene you scared me. I thought I saw an animal running across the yard. Don’t worry about it though just go back to sleep. I‘ll be back up in a minute.” 

She nodded and disappeared into the house. I stay outside for a few moments to try and make sense of what I saw. I’m definitely not tired anymore so I contemplate just sitting on the garden swing and keeping an eye out, while also just enjoying the cold weather and forest. It appeals to me. 

I go back inside and grab a blanket then head for the swing. The chains make a pleasant squeak with each push. I keep sitting there, the breeze soothing me. My eyes had finally adjusted and stars were shining bright. It was peaceful, but only for a moment. 

Rustling started in the bushes where I saw the figure run. I stand up off the swing and stare intensely at the spot. It keep rustling, getting louder. 

“Who’s there? Who are you? I have a gun you fucker!” I yell into the night. The rustling goes still. The only sound I can hear is the thumping of my heart. 

A sudden burst of noise catches me off guard and a black figure charges towards me. I gasp and start to run towards the kitchen door and shut it behind me quickly, turning the lock. I look out the window into the yard and see it. 

A large deer. Standing there confused, before taking off into the other side of the tree line. 

All of this because of a deer. He was a pretty big fucker though I’ll give him that. 

I walk back to the kitchen table and sit down, my body still shaking as the adrenaline runs through me. I tilt my head back and slow my breathing down until a smile comes across my face. I take a moment to laugh at the situation before returning back to bed. I was too worked up to try and eat anything anymore. 

The floorboards creak on the way up the stairs and down the dark hall. Again I see the window from earlier wide open. I decide to leave it as is and continue towards the room, it’s clear Sherlene was enjoying the night air. I pause outside the bedroom door and slowly grab the knob. The brass feels cool against my fingers and I slowly turn it as to not wake my wife. I creep inside as quiet as I can possibly be, right up to the bed. Lifting the sheets I make my way inside and up into Sherlene’s warmth. It didn’t take long before falling asleep again. 

“Have a good day babe, I love you.” I feel a kiss on my forehead. I open my eyes and see Sherlene in the dark room with her purse. I mumble back to her, still half asleep. She kisses me one more time before leaving the room. I hear her walk down the stairs and out the front door. A minute later he car starts and I hear the gravel crunching under the tires as she pulls out. 

The sun is hardly up and I’m too damn tired to start my day. I close my eyes and fall back asleep. 

 

.	.	. 

 

The T.V. goes dark as the credits roll . I look over to see both Mom and Sherlene asleep. They look peaceful. I gently nudge my wife, “Get up sweetie, let’s go to the bedroom.” She lets out a soft murmur and shifts around before slowly opening her eyes. A tired smile adorns her face and she stretches her arms out to me. 

“Carry me.” She whispers, leaning forward and closing her eyes. I scoop her up and bring her to my chest. Wrapping her legs  around my waist she leans into my ear. 

“I was dreaming about us Hector.” Me and you and a big happy family. We played in our grassy front yard as our kids ran through a sprinkler, laughing. Oh Hector, I didn’t want to wake up.” I felt kind of bad about disturbing her dream. Especially one that sounded so nice. Maybe one day I’ll dream like that. 

“We’re going to make those dreams come true Sherlene.” I whisper back. I feel her head weigh down on my shoulder and her legs get tighter. 

I carry her across the kitchen and into the bedroom, laying her down gently. We kiss good night and before I know it we’re both asleep.  

The next morning I wake up to soft lips against my cheek. I start smiling and run my hand over to where she’s laying, I wrap my arm around her and pull her in close, returning the favor. 

“Don’t tell me you have work today.” I said. 

“I don’t!” 

“Then why are you up so early?” 

“I wanted to get to the store early baby.” She said, kissing my cheek once again. 

“Want me to go with you?” I ask. 

“No it’s fine, maybe you and Mom could start breakfast though?” She said. 

“Yeah of course, I’ll make the biggest most tastiest breakfast all for you baby.” I said. Sherlene rolled her eyes and smiled. 

“Don’t forget about feeding yourself and Mom too.” She said. 

“Mom doesn’t need to eat baby, you need all that food if we’re gonna make that dream of yours come true!” 

“Don’t be an ass!” She said between laughs. “I gotta get going babe, love you.” 

“Love you too.” I said. We kissed one last time before she got up and walked out. Turning around and giving me a little wave before she shut the door. 

Eventually I got out of bed and went downstairs. Mom was out on the front porch, relaxing on her garden swing and reading the newspaper. The smell of fresh brewed tea wafted through the house. I went outside to sit with her and enjoy the morning. 

“Hector! I’m glad you’re up. How’d you sleep? Oh, what did you think of the movie? It was pretty good wasn’t it? Not sure why he would have left the store without his wife in the car though.” She said. 

“It was good Mom. A good pick as usual.” I sat down and saw an extra teacup set out for my. She motioned towards it, inviting me to join her. 

“Man swears to have seen UFO last night over Olmada Falls.” She read. Mom raises her eyebrows and looks at me. 

“Must’ve been one heck of a joint huh Hector.” She said. I laugh, almost spitting my tea out. These early morning newspaper readings with her will always be my favorite. 

“You know I wasn’t fully asleep last night when you left with Sherlene. I heard her talking about the dream she had.” She said. “Your father and I had that same dream, the dream that made our lives fulfilled and truly worth living.” I nod, listening intently. 

“If there’s any advice I can give you, it’s this. She’s a sweet girl, so whatever you do keep her happy. Especially when you two have kids. Always put each other first and your kids will turn out with so much love to give, since they’ll be given the perfect example.” She said. 

“And Hector. No argument is really worth fighting over.” 

“Thank you that’s pretty sound advice. Hopefully I’m not too dumb to not follow it.” I said. 

“Oh that actually reminds me, quit with the self pity,” She leans in closer, “It’s not very attractive.” She winks at me and pulls up her paper to continue reading. 

“Three arrested in attempted kidnapping of a young adult.” She read, “First of all, that’s awful. Second of all, wouldn’t that be adultnapping?” 

“I think it’s kid for every age.” I said. 

“Eh, I suppose.” She says, looking into her empty tea cup, “Oh look at that, I’m in need of a refill, I should really start brining the kettle out here.” 

“I can go run and get it real quick.” I said. 

“No, no, it’s fine, I need to keep moving anyways.” She said, standing up of the swing. She stares into the distance. “Hector?” She said, her voice growing with concern. 

“Yeah?” 

“Hector I don’t…I  feel very good.” She said. I barely opened my mouth to speak when her legs buckled beneath her. I shot up from the swing as quick as I could but it wasn’t quick enough. I watch as her body falls back onto the concrete, a stomach churning crunch hits my ears like a fucking freight train as her head slams into the ground. 

I fall to my knees and grab her head. The concrete beneath her grew dark red and a warm, wetness spread across my hands as I held her. I start to scream at her but she doesn’t answer or move. She lays there lifeless in my arms. 

I am frozen in place, not sure whether this is some kind of nightmare or not. I watch as the pool grows in size, filling cracks in the driveway. I lay her head down gently and reach into my pocket for my phone. I take it out and try to swipe in my code. It takes a few ties between the wet blood on my hands and the relentless shaking to get it open. I dial 911. I can hear myself talking but it sounds like it’s coming from someone other than me. Everything goes bright and I fall to the ground and sit there, looking at my mother, waiting for help to arrive. Even though I know it’s too late. 

 

.	.	. 

 

Loud pounding wakes me up from my nightmare. My heart almost bursts as I fling the covers aside and jump out of bed. I hear running going down the hall and a door slam close. 

I need to find a weapon! 

I rum to the closet and start pushing shirts and coats aside, looking for something I could use to defend myself. My eye catches a long wooden rod buried away in the darkness. I reach in and pull it out quickly. I look at the umbrella for a moment and decide it’s better than nothing. 

In a fewlong strides I’m at the bedroom door and opening it quick, I pop m head out and look both ways. There’s nobody there. I slowly walk out the doorway and turn towards the far end of the hallway, to the room on the opposite side of the staircase. Th floors continuously creak, making my presence known to anyone who might be inside the next room. I stop right outside the door and listen, but there’s nothing but silence. 

I gently wrap my hand around the cold door knob and slowly turn it until I hear a small click. In one quick movement I shove open the door and leap inside, the umbrella raised high over my head. 

I look around at the empty room. Everything seems fine. All the windows are shut, there’s no closets or anything, and nobody hiding under any furniture. I sigh with relief. Backing up against the wall I slide down to the floor, the umbrella resting at my feet. 

“I’ve gone crazy I guess,” I said out loud, half expecting someone to answer back at me. I sit there in silence for some time, watching the sun creep its way to the top of the sky then start its descent back down. Sherlene should be home soon. 

She’ll walk in and ask me how my day went, what I did today and all the questions that I don’t have answers for. But I can always lie. Just tell her I played the violin, walked through the garden and looked at birds. 

Yeah, I think I’ll do that, keep her in a good mood after work. I finally decide to get up off the floor after sitting there for hours. I walk back to the bedroom and put away the umbrella then head downstairs to tidy up the kitchen a little bit, that way I actually did something productive for the day. 

I look out across the yard while I wash them. I look at the spot where I saw the deer that freaked me out last night. I think about all the knocking I’ve been hearing. I think about how I snapped at Sherlene on our night out. 

I think I need professional help. 

The distress has been too long and too severe , Sherlene can only alleviate a small amount and even then she doesn’t deserve to deal with my issues. Sure I watched my Mother die and was helpless, but there’s worse things in the world, right? 

I look at the green numbers on the stove clock. She’ll be getting off work soon and heading home. I dry off my hands and go back upstairs into my practice room. The sadness in myself is profound, so much so that I can feel it physically. The weight of it crushing my heart and making my arm feel weak. I believe those stories of people who have died from broken hearts. 

I sit in the chair next to the music stand, reach underneath, and pull out the case. I flick open the latches and take out the violin. I raise the familiar instrument up to my shoulder and nestle myself into it. The bow raises above my head and I pause for a brief moment. Taking in a deep, calming breath, the bow falls down swiftly and gently onto the strings. The rhythmic motions of my wrist set into motion the music that reflects the sorrow I feel. 

I am captivated once again by the music, visuals and streams of dark colors dance in my vision as I become entranced, enthralled by the sounds. 

I hear knocking. 

I keep playing, it doesn’t matter to me, I am practically on drugs at this point. 

It grows louder. Closer. I can hear it coming down the hall. 

I don’t care the sorrowful music turns ecstatic, energy bursting in the air, the dark swirls of color in my vision replaced with a fierce red and fiery orange. 

I hear the door creak open slowly between the notes I play. Footsteps approaching. I dare not turn around, I’m too far gone. 

A cold dead hand rests itself on the violin. I slide the bow off abruptly letting out an ear piercing note and look up in panic, but nobody is there. 

With shaking hands I place the violin back in its case. With the sound of the last latch being closed something catches my attention. 

Haunting music from the garden. It sounds like my playing. I look up at the window, the daunting black drapes slowly get pulled aside on their own, revealing a cloudy night sky. I stand up and walk over to the window, what I saw froze my heart. 

Down below, in the garden, was my mother. Watching someone play the violin. I look closer and she turns her head to meet my gaze. 

“Mom?” I whisper in a trembling voice, raising my hand up to the cold glass. 

She looks at me angry then opens her mouth. The sound of a car horn echoes through the night. I stumble backwards and fall down.

### Analysis of Voice and Themes

**Capturing Your Voice:**
Your narrative voice, through the protagonist Hector, is the story's greatest strength. It feels authentic, raw, and deeply personal. Key characteristics of your voice include:

*   **Conversational and Intimate:** You speak directly to the reader ("Now before you think to yourself...") and use colloquialisms ("shit ton," "fuck that guy," "load of shit") that ground the story in a realistic, unfiltered perspective. This creates a sense of closeness, as if Hector is confiding in us.
*   **Self-Deprecating Humor:** Hector uses humor, often dark or sarcastic, to deflect from his pain. His internal monologue about his cousin Derreck or his mother's wit are examples of this coping mechanism.
*   **Introspective Turmoil:** Beneath the conversational tone lies a storm of emotion. You excel at showing Hector's internal conflict—his love for his wife versus his self-destructive tendencies, his desire to be better versus his inability to control his grief. Phrases like "I am just a burden to her, offering nothing but a broken mind" lay bare his fragile psyche.
*   **Sensory Detail:** You paint vivid pictures with sensory language—the smell of coffee, the chill of the floor, the sight of the "intimidating black" car, the sound of the train horn. This immerses the reader in Hector's world and his heightened state of awareness.

**Underlying Themes:**
The story explores several poignant and interconnected themes:

*   **Grief and Trauma:** The core of the narrative is Hector's struggle to process the traumatic death of his mother. The intrusive memories, nightmares, and flashbacks are classic symptoms of PTSD, and you portray them with painful realism.
*   **Mental Health and Sanity:** The story blurs the lines between reality, memory, and hallucination. The knocking, the shadowy figure, the deer, and the final vision of his mother in the garden all contribute to the central question of whether Hector is losing his grip on reality.
*   **The Strain on Relationships:** Grief is isolating. The story powerfully depicts how Hector's trauma strains his marriage. His emotional volatility, withdrawal, and irrational jealousy (overhearing his wife's phone call) threaten the one source of stability in his life—his wife, Sharlene.
*   **Love as an Anchor:** Despite his flaws, Hector's love for Sharlene is a constant, redeeming force. She is described as his "best friend," his "sanctuary," and the one who "cleans [his] fucked up inner world." The narrative suggests that this love is what ultimately keeps him tethered.
*   **Music as Catharsis and Curse:** For Hector, playing the violin is both a refuge and a trigger. It allows him to express his sorrow but can also plunge him into a trance-like state where he loses himself, making him vulnerable to his haunting memories.
